newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: BankBoston to handle Guatemala bond issue.
newsitem.headline: BankBoston to handle Guatemala bond issue.

text.p: The Guatemalan government selected BankBoston Corp to handle the country's first bond issue on the international market, the finance minister said on Friday.
"The selected bank is BankBoston, and the decision of the government has been communicated to the bank," Finance Minister Jose Alejandro Arevalo said at a news conference.
The bond issue will be for $150 million.
Arevalo said in the next two weeks the government and BankBoston would make presentations about the issue in Asia, Europe and the United States.
Guatemala will enter the market in late May or in June, Arevalo said.

According to Arevalo, the government plans to issue five- to 10-year bonds. The president of Guatemala's central bank, Banco de Guatemala, previously said they would be medium-term bonds maturing in three to five years.
"The interest rates will depend on the prevailing conditions of the market at the time of issue. Obviously the government would like the rate to be as low as possible," Arevalo said.
BankBoston was among five investment banks being considered by the government to handle the bond issue.
